```{python}
#| echo: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch, Rectangle

# the illustration palette (textbook/illustrations/_style.yaml)
BLUE, ORANGE, GREEN = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"
INK, MUTED, HAIR, FAINT = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#c3c2b7", "#e1e0d9"
plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 15})


def tint(c, a=0.18):
    """The color at a share a over white, as the illustrations fill a box."""
    r, g, b = (int(c[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5))
    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % tuple(round(255 - a * (255 - v)) for v in (r, g, b))


def canvas(w, h):
    """A blank figure whose coordinates are inches, so boxes are placed by eye."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(w, h))
    ax.set_xlim(0, w)
    ax.set_ylim(0, h)
    ax.axis("off")
    fig.subplots_adjust(0, 0, 1, 1)
    return fig, ax


def box(ax, x, y, w, h, text="", color=BLUE, filled=True, dashed=False, fs=15,
        weight="normal", tc=None, ha="center", family=None, lw=2):
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((x, y), w, h, boxstyle="round,pad=0,rounding_size=0.12",
                                fc=tint(color) if filled else "white", ec=color, lw=lw,
                                ls="--" if dashed else "-"))
    if text:
        tx = x + w / 2 if ha == "center" else x + 0.15
        ax.text(tx, y + h / 2, text, ha=ha, va="center", fontsize=fs, weight=weight,
                color=tc or INK, family=family, linespacing=1.3)


def arrow(ax, x1, y1, x2, y2, text="", color=MUTED, rad=0.0, fs=12, dx=0, dy=0.15, lw=2):
    ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch((x1, y1), (x2, y2), arrowstyle="-|>", mutation_scale=20,
                                 color=color, lw=lw, connectionstyle=f"arc3,rad={rad}"))
    if text:
        ax.text((x1 + x2) / 2 + dx, (y1 + y2) / 2 + dy, text, ha="center", va="bottom",
                fontsize=fs, color=color, style="italic")


def person(ax, x, y, label="you", color=MUTED):
    """A plain stick figure: the human in the picture."""
    ax.add_patch(plt.Circle((x, y + 0.62), 0.16, fc="white", ec=color, lw=2))
    ax.plot([x, x], [y + 0.46, y + 0.12], color=color, lw=2)
    ax.plot([x - 0.22, x + 0.22], [y + 0.36, y + 0.36], color=color, lw=2)
    ax.plot([x, x - 0.16], [y + 0.12, y - 0.12], color=color, lw=2)
    ax.plot([x, x + 0.16], [y + 0.12, y - 0.12], color=color, lw=2)
    ax.text(x, y - 0.32, label, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=13, color=color)


def three_rooms(n):
    """Model, chatbot, agent: the first n panels drawn, the rest left blank."""
    fig, ax = canvas(12, 4.6)
    titles = ["a language model", "a chatbot", "an agent"]
    for i in range(3):
        x0 = 0.2 + 4.0 * i
        ax.text(x0 + 1.8, 4.35, titles[i], ha="center", fontsize=17,
                weight="bold", color=INK if i < n else "white")
    # 1: text in, text out
    if n >= 1:
        box(ax, 1.0, 1.9, 2.0, 1.0, "model", BLUE, weight="bold")
        ax.text(0.45, 2.4, "text\nin", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=13, color=MUTED)
        ax.text(3.55, 2.4, "text\nout", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=13, color=MUTED)
        arrow(ax, 0.75, 2.4, 1.0, 2.4)
        arrow(ax, 3.0, 2.4, 3.25, 2.4)
        ax.text(2.0, 1.2, "no files, no terminal", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=MUTED)
    # 2: the chat window; you carry code in and out
    if n >= 2:
        box(ax, 4.7, 2.9, 2.6, 0.9, "chat window", BLUE)
        box(ax, 5.25, 3.05, 1.5, 0.0, "", BLUE, lw=0)
        person(ax, 6.0, 1.75)
        box(ax, 4.4, 0.2, 3.2, 0.7, "your files + terminal", MUTED, filled=False, fs=13)
        arrow(ax, 5.55, 2.85, 5.75, 2.5, "", BLUE)
        arrow(ax, 6.25, 2.5, 6.45, 2.85, "", BLUE)
        arrow(ax, 5.35, 1.6, 5.2, 0.95, "", ORANGE)
        arrow(ax, 6.8, 0.95, 6.65, 1.6, "", ORANGE)
        ax.text(7.75, 1.4, "you are\nthe hands", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=ORANGE, style="italic")
    # 3: the agent: model + harness + tools, acting on the files; you supervise
    if n >= 3:
        box(ax, 8.6, 2.9, 1.5, 0.9, "model", BLUE, weight="bold")
        box(ax, 10.4, 2.9, 1.5, 0.9, "harness", GREEN, weight="bold")
        arrow(ax, 10.1, 3.55, 10.4, 3.55, "", MUTED)
        arrow(ax, 10.4, 3.15, 10.1, 3.15, "", MUTED)
        ax.text(10.25, 3.95, "tool calls ⇄ results", ha="center", fontsize=12, color=MUTED, style="italic")
        box(ax, 8.6, 0.25, 3.3, 0.7, "your files + terminal", MUTED, filled=False, fs=13)
        arrow(ax, 11.15, 2.85, 11.15, 0.98, "", GREEN)
        arrow(ax, 10.85, 0.98, 10.85, 2.85, "", GREEN)
        person(ax, 9.2, 1.45, "you supervise")
        ax.text(11.55, 1.9, "the agent\nis the hands", ha="left", fontsize=13, color=GREEN, style="italic")
    plt.show()
```

# What an agent is

## A language model continues text

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.6
three_rooms(1)
```

- Claude's models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) predict what text comes next, and nothing else

## A chatbot is a model in a conversation

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.6
three_rooms(2)
```

- Ask for code and you get **text**: you run it, and you paste the error back

## An agent is a model that runs tools in a loop

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.6
three_rooms(3)
```

- **Claude Code** is the harness: the same models, with tools that act on the folder it started in

# How an agent makes changes

## A tool call is text the model writes

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.8
fig, ax = canvas(12, 4.8)
rows = [("model", "I'll check the file's columns first.", BLUE),
        ("tool call", 'Read("cohort.csv")', ORANGE),
        ("tool result", "age,e4,case   86,1,1   94,0,1   ...", GREEN),
        ("model", "Three columns. I'll count the rows with e4 = 2.", BLUE),
        ("tool call", 'Bash("python count_e4.py")', ORANGE),
        ("tool result", "41", GREEN)]
for i, (kind, text, c) in enumerate(rows):
    y = 4.05 - 0.72 * i
    ax.text(1.75, y + 0.27, kind, ha="right", va="center", fontsize=14, color=c, weight="bold")
    box(ax, 2.0, y, 7.3, 0.55, text, c, fs=14, ha="left",
        family="monospace" if kind != "model" else None)
ax.annotate("", (9.6, 0.95), (9.6, 3.45), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=HAIR, lw=1))
ax.text(9.8, 3.05, "the model writes\nthe call as text", fontsize=13, color=ORANGE, va="center", style="italic")
ax.text(9.8, 2.3, "the harness runs it\nand adds the result", fontsize=13, color=GREEN, va="center", style="italic")
ax.text(9.8, 1.55, "the model reads it\nand decides again", fontsize=13, color=BLUE, va="center", style="italic")
plt.show()
```

## Claude Code's tools: look, change, run

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.4
fig, ax = canvas(12, 4.4)
box(ax, 4.9, 1.75, 2.2, 0.85, "harness", GREEN, weight="bold")
groups = [(0.3, "look", BLUE, ["Read: a file", "Glob, Grep: find files, text", "WebFetch: a web page"]),
          (4.2, "change", ORANGE, ["Edit: part of a file", "Write: a whole file", "NotebookEdit: a cell"]),
          (8.1, "run", GREEN, ["Bash: any terminal command", "python, git, ls, ..."])]
for x, name, c, items in groups:
    y0 = 2.95 if name != "change" else 0.1
    box(ax, x, y0, 3.6, 1.35, "", c, filled=False)
    ax.text(x + 0.15, y0 + 1.1, name, fontsize=15, weight="bold", color=c, va="center")
    for j, it in enumerate(items):
        ax.text(x + 0.2, y0 + 0.75 - 0.3 * j, it, fontsize=13, color=INK, va="center")
arrow(ax, 4.95, 2.6, 3.2, 2.95, "", BLUE)
arrow(ax, 6.0, 1.8, 6.0, 1.47, "", ORANGE)
arrow(ax, 7.05, 2.6, 8.6, 2.95, "", GREEN)
ax.text(9.9, 2.2, "Bash can do anything\nyou can type in a terminal", fontsize=13, color=MUTED, ha="center", style="italic")
plt.show()
```

## You decide what the agent may do

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.6
fig, ax = canvas(11, 3.6)
acts = ["read files", "edit files", "run commands"]
modes = [("default", ["yes", "asks you", "asks you"]),
         ("accept edits", ["yes", "yes", "asks you"]),
         ("plan mode", ["yes", "no", "no"])]
col = {"yes": GREEN, "asks you": ORANGE, "no": MUTED}
for j, a in enumerate(acts):
    ax.text(3.6 + 2.5 * j, 3.15, a, ha="center", fontsize=15, weight="bold", color=INK)
for i, (m, vals) in enumerate(modes):
    y = 2.2 - 0.85 * i
    ax.text(2.2, y + 0.3, m, ha="right", va="center", fontsize=15, weight="bold", color=BLUE)
    for j, v in enumerate(vals):
        box(ax, 2.6 + 2.5 * j, y, 2.0, 0.6, v, col[v], filled=(v != "no"), fs=14)
ax.text(10.6, 1.1, "Shift+Tab\nswitches\nmodes", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=13, color=MUTED, style="italic")
plt.show()
```

- It works in **your** account, on **your** files. What it does, you did

# The agentic loop

## The loop: gather context, act, verify

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.8
fig, ax = canvas(11, 4.8)
box(ax, 4.0, 3.55, 3.0, 0.95, "gather context\nread · search · look", BLUE, fs=14)
box(ax, 7.4, 0.9, 3.0, 0.95, "act\nedit · write · run", ORANGE, fs=14)
box(ax, 0.6, 0.9, 3.0, 0.95, "verify\nrun it · check · read", GREEN, fs=14)
arrow(ax, 7.0, 4.0, 8.9, 1.9, "", MUTED, rad=-0.25)
arrow(ax, 7.4, 1.35, 3.6, 1.35, "", MUTED)
arrow(ax, 2.1, 1.9, 4.0, 4.0, "", MUTED, rad=-0.25)
box(ax, 4.3, 0.05, 2.4, 0.6, "done", MUTED, filled=False, fs=14)
arrow(ax, 2.1, 0.9, 4.3, 0.35, "", MUTED, rad=0.2)
person(ax, 5.5, 2.2, "you can interrupt")
plt.show()
```

- Round again until the task is done, or it needs you

## A workflow for bigger tasks: explore, plan, code, commit

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 3.6
fig, ax = canvas(12, 3.6)
steps = [("explore", "read the files,\nno code yet", BLUE),
         ("plan", "read its plan,\ncorrect it", BLUE),
         ("code", "write it, with\na check to run", ORANGE),
         ("commit", "save with git,\nso you can go back", GREEN)]
for i, (s, sub, c) in enumerate(steps):
    x = 0.3 + 2.95 * i
    box(ax, x, 1.2, 2.5, 1.0, s, c, weight="bold", fs=17)
    ax.text(x + 1.25, 0.85, sub, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=13, color=MUTED)
    if i < 3:
        arrow(ax, x + 2.5, 1.7, x + 2.95, 1.7)
ax.plot([0.3, 5.75], [2.55, 2.55], color=BLUE, lw=2)
ax.plot([0.3, 0.3], [2.45, 2.55], color=BLUE, lw=2)
ax.plot([5.75, 5.75], [2.45, 2.55], color=BLUE, lw=2)
ax.text(3.0, 2.7, "plan mode: reads and plans, changes nothing", ha="center", fontsize=14, color=BLUE, style="italic")
plt.show()
```

## The context window is the agent's working memory

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.4
fig, ax = canvas(12, 4.4)
items = [("your request", BLUE), ("Read cohort.csv", GREEN), ("its reply", BLUE),
         ("Bash output", GREEN), ("Read plot.py", GREEN), ("an error", ORANGE),
         ("its fix", BLUE), ("another error", ORANGE)]
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((0.6, 0.3), 3.2, 3.6, fc="white", ec=MUTED, lw=2))
for i, (t, c) in enumerate(items):
    box(ax, 0.75, 0.42 + 0.43 * i, 2.9, 0.36, t, c, fs=12)
ax.text(2.2, 4.1, "one long session", ha="center", fontsize=15, weight="bold")
ax.text(4.1, 3.6, "full: earlier details\nget lost, work drifts", fontsize=13, color=ORANGE, va="center", style="italic")
arrow(ax, 6.0, 2.1, 7.4, 2.1, "/clear", MUTED, fs=14)
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((8.0, 0.3), 3.2, 3.6, fc="white", ec=MUTED, lw=2))
box(ax, 8.15, 0.42, 2.9, 0.36, "the next task", BLUE, fs=12)
box(ax, 8.15, 0.85, 2.9, 0.36, "Read the right file", GREEN, fs=12)
ax.text(9.6, 4.1, "a fresh task", ha="center", fontsize=15, weight="bold")
plt.show()
```

- Everything the agent reads or runs takes up room. Keep one task per conversation

## Give the agent a way to check its work

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.8
fig, ax = canvas(11, 3.8)
box(ax, 0.4, 1.7, 2.4, 1.0, "act\nwrite the code", ORANGE, fs=14)
box(ax, 4.2, 1.7, 2.4, 1.0, "run the check", GREEN, fs=14, weight="bold")
box(ax, 8.2, 2.75, 2.4, 0.85, "✓  done", GREEN, fs=15)
box(ax, 8.2, 0.85, 2.4, 0.85, "✗  read the failure", ORANGE, fs=14)
arrow(ax, 2.8, 2.2, 4.2, 2.2)
arrow(ax, 6.6, 2.4, 8.2, 3.15, "passes", GREEN, fs=13)
arrow(ax, 6.6, 2.0, 8.2, 1.3, "fails", ORANGE, fs=13, dy=-0.45)
arrow(ax, 8.2, 1.05, 1.6, 1.7, "", ORANGE, rad=-0.2)
ax.text(5.0, 0.35, "try again", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=ORANGE, style="italic")
plt.show()
```

- Your notebooks' check cells are this. **The check decides what "done" means**: watch what it tests

## Now the notebook: part 3

- Ask Claude Code to write `count_motif(seq, motif)` so the check cell passes, without editing the check
- Then count TATA boxes in six promoters, and count one by hand
- About 25 minutes

## What happened in part 3

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.6
fig, ax = canvas(11, 3.6)
seq = "TATATATA"
x0, w = 2.6, 0.7
for i, ch in enumerate(seq):
    ax.text(x0 + w * i + w / 2, 1.75, ch, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=26, family="monospace", weight="bold")
for k, s in enumerate([0, 2, 4]):        # every start: three matches that overlap
    y = 2.3 + 0.32 * k
    ax.plot([x0 + w * s + 0.08, x0 + w * (s + 4) - 0.08], [y, y], color=GREEN, lw=4, solid_capstyle="round")
for k, s in enumerate([0, 4]):           # str.count jumps past each match: two
    ax.plot([x0 + w * s + 0.08, x0 + w * (s + 4) - 0.08], [1.2, 1.2], color=ORANGE, lw=4, solid_capstyle="round")
ax.text(x0 - 0.3, 2.62, "every start\nposition: 3", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=14, color=GREEN)
ax.text(x0 - 0.3, 1.2, "seq.count: 2", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=14, color=ORANGE)
ax.text(x0 + w * 8 + 0.3, 1.2, "skips past each match,\nso overlaps go missing", va="center", fontsize=13, color=ORANGE, style="italic")
plt.show()
```

- The agent did what it was asked: the request was vague, and the check tested one easy case
- The fix was a better specification, a check with the case you meant. Then the loop did the rest

# Skills

## A skill teaches Claude Code one kind of task

```{python}
#| echo: false
```

## The description decides when a skill loads

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.4
fig, ax = canvas(12, 4.4)
box(ax, 0.3, 1.8, 3.1, 0.9, '"Can you quiz me on\nodds ratios?"', MUTED, filled=False, fs=13)
cards = [("plot-house-style", "how I label my figures", False),
         ("bf550-tutor", "quiz me or explain a BF550 topic", True),
         ("git-helper", "tidy commits before a push", False)]
for i, (n, d, hit) in enumerate(cards):
    y = 3.2 - 1.15 * i
    box(ax, 4.6, y, 3.6, 0.9, f"{n}\n{d}", GREEN if hit else HAIR, filled=hit, fs=12)
arrow(ax, 3.4, 2.25, 4.6, 2.5, "matches", GREEN, fs=13)
arrow(ax, 8.2, 2.5, 8.9, 2.5, "", GREEN)
box(ax, 8.9, 0.6, 2.9, 3.4, "the full\ninstructions\nload now", GREEN, fs=14)
ax.text(6.4, 4.25, "read at start: descriptions only", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=MUTED, style="italic")
plt.show()
```

- Write the description in the words you would use: "quiz me", "practice", "explain". Restart Claude Code after a change

## The tutor you will build: `/bf550-tutor`

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.4
fig, ax = canvas(12, 4.4)
box(ax, 0.3, 1.8, 2.4, 1.0, "what do you\nwant to practise?", BLUE, fs=13)
box(ax, 3.4, 1.8, 2.4, 1.0, "reads the\nnotebook cell\nand course page", GREEN, fs=13)
box(ax, 6.5, 1.8, 2.4, 1.0, "one question\nat a time", ORANGE, fs=13)
box(ax, 9.6, 1.8, 2.2, 1.0, "what to review,\nwith links", BLUE, fs=13)
arrow(ax, 2.7, 2.3, 3.4, 2.3)
arrow(ax, 5.8, 2.3, 6.5, 2.3)
arrow(ax, 8.9, 2.3, 9.6, 2.3)
ax.annotate("", (7.2, 2.85), (8.2, 2.85), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=ORANGE, lw=2, connectionstyle="arc3,rad=1.2"))
ax.text(7.7, 3.55, "answer, feedback, harder or easier", ha="center", fontsize=12, color=ORANGE, style="italic")
srcs = [("course site", True), ("textbook", True), ("your bf550-* repos", True), ("anything private", False)]
for i, (s, ok) in enumerate(srcs):
    x = 0.3 + 3.0 * i
    box(ax, x, 0.2, 2.7, 0.6, s, GREEN if ok else MUTED, filled=ok, fs=13, tc=INK if ok else MUTED)
    if not ok:
        ax.plot([x + 0.1, x + 2.6], [0.5, 0.5], color=ORANGE, lw=2.5)
ax.plot([0.3, 8.7], [0.95, 0.95], color=GREEN, lw=2)
arrow(ax, 4.6, 0.95, 4.6, 1.8, "where it may look", GREEN, fs=12, dx=1.1, dy=0.2)
ax.text(10.7, 3.4, "on a level 1 question:\nteaches the ideas,\nnever writes the answer", ha="center", fontsize=12, color=MUTED, style="italic")
plt.show()
```

# Habits to keep

## Four habits

1. **Say what you mean.** A vague request gets a reasonable answer to a different question
2. **Give it a check.** The agent's loop is only as good as what it verifies against
3. **Read before you accept.** The transcript and the changed files are where its mistakes show
4. **You own the result.** Every question states its AI level, and what you submit is yours
